Hindsight is often used to evaluate the quality of choices made under such uncertainty, with the goal of optimizing decision-making by defining a utility function that ranks hypotheses based on their expected value. We propose an alternative approach that bypasses utility functions, using a hypothesis quality metric called 'importance' to guide decision-making instead. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this "utility-free" method by developing a new hypothesis selection algorithm and showing its performance compares favorably to existing methods in various simulation scenarios. We also examine the conditions under which the new algorithm outperforms traditional utility-based approaches. We further explore the connection between hypothesis quality and utility functions, outlining the conditions under which they align, and providing additional insights into the new hypothesis quality metric. We conclude by outlining future research directions for the "utility-free" approach.
